boutons-propos: Action verb, 17 px at 700, 48 px tall, full width by default. The dangerous one never fires alone: a confirmation box always follows it.
boutons-note: The disabled state takes a grey fill and grey text: never transparency, which would make whatever sits underneath unreadable. Pressed darkens the fill of the primary and dangerous buttons, and lays a light background under the secondary and quiet ones.
bouton-etats-propos: The active state serves controls that toggle: the word does not change, the fill says it, and the control announces itself as pressed.
bouton-chargement: Waiting — disabled button and spinning arc
bouton-chargement-note: Waiting is not a button variant: it is a disabled button carrying an arc. The component therefore knows a single way of being unactionable.
bouton-lien: Link button — it leads elsewhere instead of acting
largeurs-propos: A lone action takes the whole width. Two actions share the line: back on the left, the main action on the right — that is the system's rule, not a setting.
onglets-filtre-propos: They filter a list in place, under the header: 48 px tall, 17 px label, 3 px rule under the active tab.
onglets-filtre-defile: When room runs short, the row alone scrolls and the active tab is brought into view
pilules-propos: 40 px of drawing inside a 48 px target. Chosen: solid fill. Disabled: grey border, no fill.
pilule-decochable: Removable — the tick says it can be taken off
pilule-chevron: With chevron — it opens a choice sheet and toggles nothing
pilule-note: The pill stays at 15 px, its original size: divergences 6 and 15 raise the filter tab and the segmented control to 17, not it.
segmente-propos: A single choice among three or four, all visible. The whole group is one tab stop, and the arrow keys move from segment to segment.
segmente-note: Three or four segments at most: beyond that the labels crowd and the choice stops being readable at a glance.
